title: Generic Policy Engine Returning Opaque "Does Not Meet Policy" Errors
pattern: A policy evaluation, validation, or compliance engine returns a single, generic "does not meet policy" error without including specific detail about which rules failed or the mismatched values.
why_bad: Awkward user experience. When a deployment or validation is rejected, operators are left confused and must manually inspect database states or trace internal code execution to figure out the fix.
detection: A policy enforcement point returns constant, unparameterized error variants upon failing complex conditional validation chains.
counterexample: Simple, low-level binary validation checkers where any failure simply means "corrupt input." Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix:
Structure the policy engine to yield descriptive, actionable feedback identifying the exact rule violation and the observed vs. expected attributes.
```rust
pub struct PolicyViolation {
    pub rule_name: String,
    pub expected: String,
    pub observed: String,
}
```
source: Google SRE, *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* (2020), Chapter 14, "Deploying Code", p. 114, 370.
